tossups.text: In human physiology, this structure is essential for appendicular skeleton. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in appendicular skeleton.

tossups.text: This process conserves the V minus A current according to a theory of it which superseded the four fermion contact theory. The Kurie plot is used to analyse the energy spectrum of this process, which was studied by Chien-Shiung Wu in cobalt-60. Electron capture is the inverse of this process, whose main radiative emission exhibits a distribution of kinetic energies that prompted Wolfgang Pauli to suggest the existence of the neutrino. For 10 points, name this weak force process that converts neutrons to protons by emitting electrons.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for villi and microvilli. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this duodenum-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The duodenum is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in villi and microvilli.

tossups.text: Sulfonating this compound creates the water-soluble compound TPPTS. Chloride, carbon monoxide, and two of this molecule are the four ligands for one compound that reacts reversibly with dioxygen and dihydrogen and has a central iridium atom. Three molecules of it are ligands in a 16-electron rhodium-containing homogeneous catalyst for hydrogenation. In addition to Vaska's complex and Wilkinson's catalyst, this molecule with a cone angle of 145 degrees reacts with diethylazodicarboxylate to form an intermediate that activates the oxygen atom of an alcohol as a leaving group in the Mitsunobu reaction, and converts azides to primary amines in the Staudinger reaction. It reacts with an alkyl halide, then with a strong base, to generate a phosphorane commonly used in a reaction that may proceed through a betaine intermediate. For 10 points, name this bulky phosphine used in the Wittig reaction.

Large ritual objects made of this material called intihuatana ("in-tee-wah-TAH-nah") served as metaphorical "hitching posts" of the sun to which maidens were tied during the Raymi festival. This material was used to create a race of dumb giants, who were then washed away and replaced by a second generation of humans created by the Inca god Viracocha ("vee-rah-KOH-chah"). Debunked theories suggests that large objects made of this material imply the presence of pre-Columbian Chinese or African rulers in present-day Tabasco province. The open mouth of the god Tonatiuh ("toh-nah-TEE-ooh") is shown at the center of a round Aztec object made of this material which contains a ritual calendar and represents the sun. The Olmecs carved giant heads out of, for 10 points, what general material that composes the Andes?

This author often used the phrase "rosy-fingered dawn" to describe the passage of time, and described the sea as "wine-dark," instead of blue. In a section titled for the "Rage" of one character, this author described how he returned to battle in response to the death of his friend, Patroclus. At the end of one text, this author described a man reuniting with his wife Penelope in Ithaca, and in another, this author narrated the story of the Trojan Horse. For 10 points, name this ancient Greek poet credited with writing the Odyssey and the Iliad.

This man's sons were called "Blitomammas" or "cabbage suckers." He was mocked as "squill head," possibly a reference to his long head. His illegitimate son and namesake was executed for failing to pick up survivors after the Battle of Arginusae. This man's mistress was the Milesian woman Aspasia. In one speech, this man noted "if we look to the laws, they afford equal justice to all in their private differences" before describing the society he led as one thrown open "to the world" as "the school of Hellas." As leader, he commissioned Phidias to build various monuments, including one at the Temple of Zeus. This man gave a noted funeral oration before dying of plague during the Peloponnesian War. For 10 points, name this leader during the "Golden Age of Athens."

In this year, a man gave a speech that began by stressing he was speaking "not as a Massachusetts man, nor as a Northern man, but as an American." In this year of the Seventh of March speech, Southerners met to potentially discuss secession at the Nashville Convention. In this year, Henry Foote drew a pistol on Thomas Hart Benton. The declaration that there was a "higher law than the Constitution" is from a speech given in this year by William Seward. In this year, following the death of Zachary Taylor, Stephen Douglas arranged for the passage of a harsher Fugitive Slave Law in exchange for concessions to the anti-slavery factions. For 10 points, identify this year whose namesake compromise allowed California to enter the Union as a free state.

This woman married Rhadamanthys after going to the Islands of the Blest. Before sleeping with her first husband, she demanded that he avenge the deaths of her brothers by attacking the Taphians and Teleboans. This woman was allowed to give birth after her servant-girl Galanthis tricked Lucina into releasing her curse. In later life, she was persecuted by Eurystheus, but obtained vengeance by gouging the eyes out of his head. She gave birth to Iphicles by her first husband, Amphitryon, but gave birth to a more famous child by a god who took that husband's form to seduce her. For 10 points, name this mother of Heracles.

To oppose this process, Senator Harry Byrd headed a campaign of "Massive resistance." This process was ordered to be carried out "with all deliberate speed" following a 1954 Supreme Court case that ruled that the notion of "separate but equal" was unconstitutional. The ruling in Brown v. Board of Education called for, for 10 points, what process that ended the separation of education institutions based on race?

In human physiology, this structure is essential for stomach anatomy. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this esophagus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The esophagus is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in stomach anatomy.

tossups.text: Carciplexes ("CAR-sih-plex-iz") are used to prevent [4]annulene ("four ANN-yoo-leen") from dimerizing via this reaction, which is used to trap benzyne ("BEN-zyne") intermediates. A "retro-" version of this reaction can occur in mass spectrometry. A methyl vinyl ketone was used in this reaction by Breslow ("BRESS-loh") to show that it undergoes hydrophobic acceleration. Dihydropyran ("dy-HY-dro-PIE-ran") derivatives are synthesized by replacing one reactant in this reaction with an aldehyde. This reaction preferentially forms 1,2- or 1,4-products. The transition state of this reaction maximizes the overlap between HOMO and LUMO by pointing the electron-withdrawing groups of one reactant inward in the endo configuration. For 10 points, name this reaction in which cyclohexene derivatives are formed from a 4-plus-2 cycloaddition between dienes and dienophiles.

The "Y" fumarole on this peak is the type locality of the extremely rare exhalative minerals ziesite and blossite, which are water-soluble copper-vanadium minerals. Cerro Chino rises to the east of this mountain, and the San Marcelano (san mar-se-LA-no) vents lie to its northeast. The southeastern and southwestern extensions of Cerro Verde National Park surround this mountain which inspired the triangular shape of its nation's coat of arms. A novel of Claribel Alegría is titled for the "Ashes of" this mountain which anchors a description of that country's Pipil genocide. Lake Coatepeque (kwa-te-PE-ke) lies northeast of this peak, and the ruins of the buried village of Matazano (ma-ta-SA-no) lie to its south. This member of the Cordillera de Apaneca (kor-di-YE-ra de a-pa-NE-ka), which featured on the now defunct 10-colon banknote, is located just inside the border of the Sonsonate (son-so-NA-te) Department. For 10 points, name this Salvadoran volcano, part of the Santa Ana Complex, known as the "lighthouse of the Pacific," the most active in Central America.

Years after dueting with Meatloaf, Ellen Foley had a supporting role on this show as Billie Young. She was replaced after the show's second season, as was the late Selma Diamond. Diamond's replacement, Florence Halop, likewise died after the third season and was replaced by Marsha Warfield as the tough bailiff Roz. Other characters included Christine Sullivan, played by Markie Post, and Dan Fielding, played by John Larroquette. For 10 points name this long running sitcom that featured Harry Anderson as Judge Harold T. Stone, presiding.

This poet is invaded by night "with her powerful army" in a poem that recalls being armed for the "hour of revenge." A poem by this author asks a "brother" in the "bedrock depths" to "rise up in birth with me." The memory of a "deserted one" is likened to the sea at the end of a numeralled collection by this poet that opens with "Body of a Woman." This poet climbs the title "Heights" of a ruined city in a poem from a fifteen-canto epic chronicling the New World. This poet grieves a former lover in the last romantic poem of a collection, which opens by declaring "tonight I can write the saddest lines." For 10 points, Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair is by what Chilean poet?

One of this artist's works was the Anglo-Japanese style Peacock room commissioned by Frederick Leyland. This artist painted his mistress Joanna Hiffernan - a woman with red hair dressed in all-white standing on a wolf-skin in front of a white curtain with a lily in hand. Besides his Symphony in White, No. 1: The White Girl, this man depicted fireworks in London in his Nocturne in Black and Gold. His most famous work is a portrait of his mother seated facing left, with her hands in her lap, and is painted with the two title colors. For 10 points, name this artist of An Arrangement in Grey and Black.

The author of this play discussed his decision to have a character instantaneously respond to a whistle in the second volume of his Theatrical Notebooks. A character in this play tells a bad joke about a slow-working tailor, then repeatedly asks for a sugarplum, after recalling a boating accident on Lake Como. This play's set includes two high windows resembling eyes. A character throws away a three-legged toy dog and puts on his bloodstained "old stancher" handkerchief at the end of this play, which opens with another character moving a stepladder back and forth. After losing their legs in a biking accident, an elderly couple in this play live inside dustbins. Nagg and Nell appear alongside the wheelchair-using Hamm and his servant Clov in, for 10 points, what play by Samuel Beckett?

this structure is essential for joint movements. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this synovial-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The synovial is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in joint movements.

tossups.text: The 1938 Nobel Peace Prize was given to a group who issued this kind of document to refugees. Travelers to Mecca may have a hajj version of this document. American documents of this come with 32 pages for visas. For 10 points, name these documents one must have to travel internationally.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for carbon dioxide transport. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this diffusion-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The diffusion is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in carbon dioxide transport.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with inspiration and expiration.
What is the main function of the diaphragm in the respiratory system?
Name another component of the respiratory system related to inspiration and expiration.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human respiratory system.

parts.text: Give this term for the general shape that a mineral takes when it crystallizes. Examples of this property include botryoidal, describing the grape-like appearance of hematite, and acicular, describing the needle-like appearance of rutile in quartz.

This group of silicate minerals names a habit characterized by strong and flexible hairlike fibers. These minerals were widely used in insulation until it was discovered that their inhalation can cause lung cancer and mesothelioma.
This is the term for a pseudomorph that grows on the original mineral, with the original mineral sometimes dissolving to create a hollow space known as a "cast."

bonuses.leadin: Pseudomorphs are formed when a mineral adopts this macroscopic property of another mineral. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with thymus gland.
What is the main function of the lymph in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to thymus gland.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Identify this non-linear PDE that relates the difference in capillary pressure across the interface of two static fluids.

The Young-Laplace equation thus also governs the formation of these entities, which consist of gas pockets trapped in liquids, as in carbonated beverages. Sound waves excited these entities into emitting light in the 100% legit physics phenomenon of sonoluminescence.

This man names a simple first order equation used to predict the acoustic motion of bubbles along with Milton Plesset. He is also the first namesake of a dynamic boundary condition between two fluids of different densities, which often results in the creation of "fingers" seen in famous nebulae.

bonuses.leadin: Adding a boundary condition such as a contact angle to this equation allows it to describe meniscus formation in a tube. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Figures like Castor and Pollux, Laertes, Atalanta, and Theseus all were members of this mythical crew who sought the fleece.
Along the way, Hylas, the servant of this Argonaut, was kidnapped by water nymphs. This Argonaut searched for Hylas for a long time before returning to complete his twelve labors.
The Argonauts stopped at this city near the modern-day-country of Georgia, where Jason was aided by the king's sorceress daughter Medea in completing three tasks in exchange for the fleece.

bonuses.leadin: For ten points each, answer some questions about Jason and the quest for the Golden Fleece:

parts.text: Name this man from Greek mythology who journeyed to the Underworld to retrieve his dead wife Eurydice, but failed the trial after he turned to look back at her.
Orpheus used music to drown out these birdlike women's alluring song for the Argonauts. Odysseus tied himself to a mast so he could hear them without getting eaten.
Using music from his lyre, Orpheus brought this daughter of Demeter and wife of Hades to tears. Her time in the Underworld for half the year causes winter.

bonuses.leadin: He was torn apart by Maenads for playing miserable music after his most famous venture. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Egyptian god of the sun who battled against the serpent god Apophis.

Ra sent the goddess Sekhmet, who is represented as one of these animals, to Earth as an embodiment of his rage to punish humanity's impiety. These animals were also represented by Sekhmet's sister Bastet.
Sekhmet's bloodlust was only stopped when Ra gave a red version of this substance to her, after which she transformed back into the cow goddess Hathor.

bonuses.leadin: This deity piloted the solar barque through the sky and the underworld in a mythological representation of the day-night cycle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this empire at the westernmost edge of Africa, centered in present-day Senegal. Alternatively, you may identify the similarly named, extant ethnic group that dominated it.

The explorer Juan Garrido ("guh-REE-doh") was born in this African kingdom, which conducted a major Atlantic slave trade with Portugal. Afonso I ruled this kingdom, which shares its name with a river.

According to the historian al-Umari, Mansa Musa's predecessor sponsored a great Atlantic voyage, speculated to have found the Americas. You may name either the man often credited with sponsoring that voyage, who is not listed as a mansa, OR the mansa who precedes Musa in most official records.

bonuses.leadin: This empire's deposed ruler Bumi Jeleen converted from Islam to Catholicism upon visiting Portugal, but was killed by a Portuguese captain on the return trip. For 10 points each:

parts.text: These birds can cause storms merely by flapping their huge wings. Their archnemeses are whales.
Like Raven, this canine figure is most often portrayed as a trickster. In one story, he plays a hilarious trick called the Vomit Exchange on Owl.

These creatures appear in many variations of the Sedna myth. In one story, Sedna's father forces her to marry one of these birds, but she runs away, which then forces her father to cut her fingers off.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name some creatures from Native American myth that don't show up much in other myth systems.

parts.text: Name this emperor of an Asian country that fought against the US in the Pacific Theatre of World War II.
Hirohito was an emperor of this country. Its cities of Hiroshima and Nagasaki were attacked by atomic bombs that forced their surrender.

A pivotal battle during the Pacific Theatre was this one, taking place in an atoll at the end of the Hawaiian island chain, in which American forces sank four Japanese carriers. An airport in Chicago is named for it.

bonuses.leadin: This emperor gave the "Jewel Voice Broadcast" to announce his country's surrender in World War II. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with stress response.
What is the main function of the adrenal in the endocrine system?
Name another component of the endocrine system related to stress response.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human endocrine system.

parts.text: Name this process in which two light atomic nuclei are combined to form a single heavier nucleus.
Developed by its namesake British scientist, this measure relates ion density and confinement time, and is a minimum condition for productive fusion.
Intended to generate 500 megawatts of fusion power, this tokamak will be located in Cadarache, France.

bonuses.leadin: It can be created in a device named for Philo Farnsworth and Robert Hirsch. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this river that defines the border between Texas and four Mexican states.
A series of killings termed feminicidio have taken place in this city on the Rio Grande, which is home to hundreds of maquiladoras. The Bridge of the Americas connects it to El Paso.

This city near the mouth of the Rio Grande lies across it from the Mexican city of Matamoros. In 1906, 167 African-American soldiers stationed near this city were dishonorably discharged after they were falsely accused of a pair of shootings.

bonuses.leadin: The Big Bend National Park is named for the arc that this river cuts during its journey into the Gulf of Mexico. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This agreement admitted Maine as a free state and its namesake as a slave state. It also outlawed slavery above the 36' 30" line in the former Louisiana territory, except in the namesake state.
Stephen Douglas designed this 1854 act, which allowed popular sovereignty within certain territories to decide the slavery question before statehood. It effectively repealed the Missouri Compromise.

During the "Bleeding Kansas" period, pro-slavery settlers drafted this failed constitution for the state of Kansas as a response to the Topeka one. President Buchanan endorsed it, but Stephen Douglas did not.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer some questions about slavery in the territories before the American Civil War.

parts.text: Name this author of the collection Fatal Interview, who Parker said "made poetry seem so easy that we could all do it." The speaker says, "heroes seek release / From dusty bondage into luminous air" in a sonnet by this author.

Dorothy Parker wrote about how one of these objects "gives a single light" in her poem "Interview." In Millay's poem "First Fig," one of these objects "burns at both ends" and "will not last the night."

Parker wrote a poem about a "Perfect" one of these objects, which sometimes title a Millay poem that describes "the air incarnadine." These objects are repeated in a line from Gertrude Stein's poem "Sacred Emily."
acceptableAnswers: “No rose that in a garden ever grew”
“a rose is a rose is a rose is a rose”

bonuses.leadin: Dorothy Parker said that she followed in the "exquisite" footsteps of this author "unhappily in my own horrible sneakers." For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Contarelli Chapel contains three paintings by Caravaggio depicting scenes from the life of this saint, one of the 12 Apostles and the Four Evangelists. A light floods in from the upper right corner in the "Calling" of this man.
A fresco by Michelangelo on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel shows this man touching fingers with God after his creation.
Art depicting the "Rest on the Flight into" this modern-day country typically show Mary and Joseph cuddling an infant Jesus. The Holy Family flees to this location after hearing of Herod's decree.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Biblical scenes as they are depicted in art, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this author of Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead. This winner of the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature wrote the massive 2014 historical novel The Books of Jacob.

Several chapters of Drive Your Plow begin with a quotation from Blake's poem "Auguries of Innocence," which opens "To see a World in [this object]." A Wisława Szymborska ("veesh-WAH-vuh sheem-BOR-skuh") poem titled "View With [this object]" declares "It does just fine without a name."
Wisława Szymborska and Olga Tokarczuk are from this country, whose national epic is Adam Mickiewicz's ("meets-KYEH-vitch's") Pan Tadeusz (tuh-DOOZE").

bonuses.leadin: The narrator of this author's best-known novel translates William Blake with her friend Dizzy. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with allergies and hypersensitivity.
What is the main function of the vaccine in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to allergies and hypersensitivity.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this sacrament, called "chrismation" in Eastern Orthodoxy, in which a baptized young person sealstheir covenant with God and, in some Christian sects, becomes a full member of the church.
Another Catholic sacrament requires believers to visit priests and perform this ritual of privately explainingtheir sins and asking for forgiveness.
To complete the repentance required of confession, Catholics are often required to perform prayers andreflect on holy "mysteries" using this set of prayer beads, which is divided into decades.

bonuses.leadin: Catholicism recognizes seven sacraments, major events in the life of a member of the church such asbaptism and last rites. For ten points each,

What is the main function of the pharynx in the respiratory system?
